Known Issues and Limitations

Known issues

  • Target sizes below 1 GiB fail for large arrays. Dispatcher.createTarForChunk computes the number of tarballs in whole GiB (divmod(int(size), int(targetSize))), so a target size below 1 GiB raises ZeroDivisionError when an array exceeds the target size.

  • A metadata file larger than the target size fails. The distributor treats it like a large array and passes it to createTarForChunk, which expects a directory. This can happen with the consolidated metadata (.zmetadata, or the root zarr.json) of a large store with many groups.

  • dispatch(freq, zoomLevel, subGroupID) fails for split stores. It selects the subgroups of a store by the store name <experiment>_<frequency>_<zoom>, which it reads from the path of the first member of each subgroup. The members of var and chunk subgroups are named relative to the store (e.g. tas), so this raises IndexError; for an array in a nested group (e.g. z2/ocean/sst) it reads a group name instead and silently selects nothing. dispatchStoreToTarStores is not affected.

  • One zoom level per store. dispatch relies on the naming convention of one HEALPix zoom level per store, so a store holding several zoom levels as groups cannot be archived per zoom level.

  • Unclosed reference files. convertKerchunkReferenceFilesOfZarrStoreToParquet writes and reads the *_Offset_kerchunk.json.copy files without closing them. This works because CPython closes them immediately, and shows as ResourceWarning in the tests.

Limitations

  • Kerchunk references are zarr v2. zarr v3 stores are referenced through a translation of their metadata to zarr v2; codecs without a zarr v2 equivalent (transpose, chained compressors) raise a ValueError. See Store Layouts.

  • Fill values of translated zarr v3 arrays. xarray keeps the fill value of zarr v3 arrays in the _FillValue attribute. An array without it but with a non-zero zarr fill value keeps that fill value in the zarr v2 references, where xarray treats it as missing data; a warning is logged.

  • Nested groups need consolidated metadata. Parquet references of a store with nested groups must be opened with consolidated=True: fsspec’s listing of parquet references does not find nested groups.

  • Shards are not split. A single shard larger than the target size makes a tarball larger than the target size.

  • Unsupported sharding. Nested sharding, a codec after sharding_indexed and shard index codecs other than bytes with an optional crc32c raise a ValueError.

Worked around

  • Missing chunks in parquet references (fsspec). When fsspec stores the URLs of an array’s references as a pandas categorical (by default when an array has at least 10 references per URL, i.e. nearly every array of a tarball), a chunk missing from the references reads back as [nan] instead of as missing. zarr does not write chunks that hold only the fill value, so this gave wrong data. zarrcurator writes the parquet references without categoricals (categorical_threshold=sys.maxsize).
